patient.chief_complaint: Three months of rapidly progressive bilateral leg weakness, foot drop, and difficulty with arm elevation
patient.history_present_illness: Angela Rosario is a 42-year-old nurse who presents to urgent neurology clinic with a 3-month history of rapidly progressive bilateral leg weakness. The symptoms began with right foot drop that developed over 1 week, followed by left foot weakness 3 weeks later. She now has difficulty raising her arms above shoulder height and reports bilateral grip weakness. She is considering stopping work as an ICU nurse due to difficulty carrying equipment. She reports associated diffuse myalgia, fatigue, and proximal arm aching. She was evaluated in her own ED 6 weeks ago with labs showing markedly elevated CK (4,800 U/L), and was told she may have 'some kind of muscle problem' and to follow up with neurology. She was empirically started on a 5-day prednisone taper by her primary care physician, which gave modest temporary improvement but symptoms recurred within 2 weeks. She notes her eyelids are slightly heavy, particularly at the end of long shifts, though no diplopia. She has had some difficulty swallowing solids over the past 4 weeks. She recently completed a 6-week course of atorvastatin 40 mg (started 4 months ago) before suspending it herself after reading about statin myopathy. A prior EMG ordered by her primary care was interpreted as 'neuropathic' by the technician (not a physician) and she was told to see neurology for neuropathy — but she suspects this is wrong given her muscle symptoms.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Anti-synthetase syndrome (anti-Jo-1 inflammatory myopathy ± interstitial lung disease) — misattributed to peripheral neuropathy

differential.key_features: Recent atorvastatin; persists despite statin discontinuation; anti-HMGCR positive.
Heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, skin features absent here; anti-Mi-2 / anti-TIF1γ.
Symmetric proximal weakness, elevated CK, endomysial CD8 infiltrate.
Proximal weakness can mimic; need AChR antibodies and RNS/SFEMG; bulbar/ocular features here are absent.
EMG showed myopathic, not neurogenic, MUPs; sensory exam intact — this is NOT peripheral neuropathy.

tool_parameters.query: anti-synthetase syndrome interstitial lung disease HRCT

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Recognize this is NOT a peripheral neuropathy — EMG shows myopathic motor unit potentials and sensory exam is intact
Send CK, aldolase, myositis-specific antibody panel (anti-Jo-1, anti-HMGCR, etc.)
Screen for interstitial lung disease (chest HRCT, PFTs)
Initiate corticosteroids ± methotrexate / rituximab once diagnosis confirmed
contraindicated_actions: Do not treat as peripheral neuropathy — diagnosis is muscle disease
Do not restart statin if anti-HMGCR positive (IMNM)
key_reasoning_points: Short-duration low-amplitude polyphasic MUPs with early recruitment = MYOPATHIC pattern, not neurogenic
Normal NCS + intact sensory exam excludes peripheral neuropathy
Anti-synthetase syndrome (especially anti-Jo-1) features myositis + ILD + Raynaud's + mechanic's hands + arthritis

red_herrings.data_point: Case is labeled 'peripheral neuropathy' and presented as such
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: EMG shows myopathic units; the working diagnosis is myositis, not neuropathy.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on statin myalgia / simple myopathy
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Statin discontinuation should resolve simple statin myopathy; persistence suggests autoimmune (anti-HMGCR IMNM) or anti-synthetase syndrome.
